paper_metadata.title: Portfolio rebalancing experiments using the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz

summary: The paper studies 8-stock portfolio rebalancing on an idealized gate-model simulator using QAOA in two forms: soft-constraint QAOA and hard-constraint QAOA (Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz). It reports 16 logical qubits for the 8-asset two-spin encoding, p = 1 single-circuit sweeps, and a 6-month rebalancing campaign with p = 2, 3, 4; the hard-constraint variant achieved 100% feasible solutions in the single-portfolio experiment and was reported to reach within 5% of optimal adjusted returns in the multi-period campaign, but no practical quantum advantage was demonstrated.

experiments.description: Single-period portfolio rebalancing on 8 ASX stocks using soft-constraint QAOA with penalty term, evaluated on an idealized gate-model simulator.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset: each asset position z_i is represented by long/short binary variables x_i^+, x_i^- (equivalently spins s_i^+, s_i^-), giving 2 qubits per asset.
problem_formulation.objective_function: C_soft(s) = C_RR(s) + C_TC(s) + P_INV(s), where C_RR is the Markowitz risk-return term, C_TC is fixed trading cost, and P_INV = A(Σ_i z_i - D)^2 enforces the investment constraint.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft penalty term for investment constraint; standard QAOA mixer over all qubits.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising cost operator obtained by substituting Pauli-Z operators for spins in C_soft(s).

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio rebalancing for a small 8-stock portfolio with target holding D=4 lots.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily returns; average daily returns and covariance matrix computed from 252 trading days; later annualized by multiplying average returns and covariance by 250 for scaling

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily average returns and covariance matrix computed from 2017 daily stock returns; for the scaling experiment, daily averages and covariances were annualized by multiplying by 250.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single p=1 circuit sweep over beta and gamma; expectation value landscape examined visually.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Brute-force calculation of penalty scaling bound A > max[C(s)] - min[C(s)] and data scaling analysis.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expectation values and feasible-solution behavior analyzed from simulator outputs.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 16 logical qubits, p = 1, idealized simulator only
limiting_factors: No classical runtime comparison establishing advantage

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states an idealized simulator of a gate-model quantum computer and does not name a specific simulator type.
16 qubits inferred from 8 assets × 2 spin variables per asset.
Speedup order not characterized in the paper; only tractability and qualitative performance are discussed.
The paper reports simulator-based exploration of a single p=1 circuit and does not claim demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Single-period portfolio rebalancing on 8 ASX stocks using hard-constraint QAOA / Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz with parity-ring mixers, evaluated on an idealized gate-model simulator.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz with hard-constraint parity-ring mixers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset with long/short variables; hard constraint enforced by parity mixers on long and short registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: C_hard(s) = C_RR(s) + C_TC(s), with investment constraint enforced by mixer design rather than penalty.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard constraint via two parity-ring mixers acting on long and short variables plus entangled initial state; feasible subspace only.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising cost operator obtained by substituting Pauli-Z operators for spins in C_hard(s).

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio rebalancing for a small 8-stock portfolio with target holding D=4 lots.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily returns; average daily returns and covariance matrix computed from 252 trading days; later annualized by multiplying average returns and covariance by 250 for scaling

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily average returns and covariance matrix computed from 2017 daily stock returns; for the scaling experiment, daily averages and covariances were annualized by multiplying by 250.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single p=1 circuit sweep over beta and gamma; expectation value landscape examined visually; compared against soft-constraint QAOA.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construction of feasible initial state and parity mixers; penalty scaling bound used for comparison experiments.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expectation values and feasible-solution behavior analyzed from simulator outputs.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 16 logical qubits, p = 1, idealized simulator only
limiting_factors: No runtime or scaling advantage shown

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states an idealized simulator of a gate-model quantum computer and does not name a specific simulator type.
16 qubits inferred from 8 assets × 2 spin variables per asset.
Speedup order not characterized in the paper; only qualitative performance is discussed.
The paper reports 100% feasible-solution probability for the hard-constraint formulation on the simulator, but this is not a demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Comparison of soft-constraint QAOA and hard-constraint QAOA on a single 8-stock portfolio using annualized returns, with p=2,3,4 and 20 random seeds per configuration.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA (soft constraints) and QAOA with hard-constraint parity mixers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset; 16-qubit register for 8 assets. Soft formulation uses penalty term; hard formulation uses parity mixers and feasible initial state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft penalty vs hard constraint via XY/parity mixers and entangled initial state.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising cost operator from C_soft or C_hard after Pauli-Z substitution.

problem_instance.description: Single-portfolio evaluation on 8 ASX stocks with annualized returns and D=4 target lots.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: annualized returns and covariance matrix obtained by multiplying daily averages and covariances by 250

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily average returns and covariance matrix annualized by multiplying by 250 to improve QAOA scaling.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 randomly seeded simulated runs per configuration; cumulative probability distributions of cost over all solutions and over feasible solutions; compared to brute-force baseline and random feasible draw.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Annualization of input data; brute-force baseline generation; feasible-solution statistics.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Cumulative probability plots for all solutions and feasible solutions; comparison to brute force and random feasible selection.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 16 logical qubits, p = 2, 3, 4, 20 random seeds per configuration, simulator only
limiting_factors: Classical brute force used only as a benchmark on a small instance
Results are limited to 8 assets and 6 monthly steps

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states an idealized simulator of a gate-model quantum computer and does not name a specific simulator type.
16 qubits inferred from 8 assets × 2 spin variables per asset.
p values explicitly reported as 2, 3, and 4; num_layers recorded as the maximum depth used in this experiment.
Speedup order not characterized in the paper.
The paper claims qualitative performance advantages for the hard-constraint QAOA on the simulator, but not a practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Multi-period monthly portfolio rebalancing over 6 months using soft-constraint QAOA and hard-constraint QAOA, with trading costs included and comparison to brute-force trajectories.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA (soft constraints) and QAOA with hard-constraint parity mixers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset; 16-qubit register for 8 assets. Soft formulation uses penalty term; hard formulation uses parity mixers and feasible initial state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Monthly rebalancing objective based on C_RR and C_TC, with soft or hard investment constraint handling.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft penalty vs hard constraint via parity mixers and entangled initial state.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising cost operator from C_soft or C_hard after Pauli-Z substitution.

problem_instance.description: Six-month rebalancing scenario with monthly optimization, using annualized returns computed independently for each of the first 6 months of 2017.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: monthly annualized returns computed independently for each month; covariance and returns scaled to annualized values; trading cost T=0.015

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Annualized returns computed independently for each of the first 6 months of 2017; A set to 2.5 due to larger extrema in monthly statistics; trading cost included at T=0.015.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared QAOA variants against brute-force optimal trajectory over 6 monthly rebalancing steps; metrics: number of trades, adjusted portfolio returns, and average risk.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Monthly annualization of returns; brute-force trajectory computation; metric aggregation over 6 months.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Trade counts, adjusted returns, and average risk plotted and compared to brute force.

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states an idealized simulator of a gate-model quantum computer and does not name a specific simulator type.
16 qubits inferred from 8 assets × 2 spin variables per asset.
p values explicitly reported as 2 and 4; num_layers recorded as the maximum depth used in this experiment.
Speedup order not characterized in the paper.

experiments.description: Multi-period portfolio rebalancing over 6 months using QAOA soft-constraint formulation, evaluated on an idealized gate-model simulator.
key_results: Compared against brute force over 6 monthly rebalancing steps
Adjusted returns and average risk were reported over 6 months
Results were close to optimal in the reported campaign

experiments.description: Multi-period portfolio rebalancing over 6 months using QAOA hard-constraint formulation (Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz), evaluated on an idealized gate-model simulator.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz with hard-constraint parity mixers

key_results: Returned feasible solutions with 100% probability in the single-portfolio experiment
For the 6-month campaign, p = 4 achieved the best adjusted returns and optimal risk when directed to minimize risk
Outperformed the soft-constraint QAOA in the reported comparisons
